description.value: A voxel-based morphometry study comparing gray matter volume between recent onset PTSD patients and trauma-exposed survivors without PTSD after a coal mine flood disaster.

spans.text: The goal of this study is to use both VBM and region of interest (ROI) methods to determine whether regional gray matter and white matter volumes and density of a group of recent onset PTSD patients who were trapped for 72 h in a coal mine for 72 h due to a coal mine flood disaster are different from those of a control group without PTSD but who experienced the same disaster.

spans.text: The main findings of this study are that in survivors of a coal mine flood disaster with recent onset PTSD, there is a significant decrease in regional gray matter volume and signal intensity in the left hippocampus, left parahippocampal gyrus and bilateral calcarine cortex, and that there is no significant change in regional white matter volume compared with survivors without PTSD.

description.value: VBM preprocessing including spatial normalization, segmentation, intensity modulation, and spatial smoothing.

spans.text: In this approach, the individual MRI scans were spatially normalised from native space to the Montreal Neurological Institute 152-image template with a 12-parameter affine transformation with 16 nonlinear iterations and a 25-mm nonlinear basis function cutoff. Normalised images were then segmented with signal intensity and prior probability information.
VBM image analysis was performed on a computer workstation with MATLAB 7.01 and VBM2 software

Intensity modulation was performed on the optimally normalised segmented gray matter MRI scans by increasing or reducing voxel intensity, depending on whether the surrounding voxels were compressed or expanded in the normalisation process.
Modulated gray matter images were smoothed with a 12-mm full width at half maximum isotropic Gaussian kernel before analysis with voxel-wise group comparisons.
